title: U.S. House · Ohio's 7th District
area: Northeast Ohio, including parts of Cuyahoga, Lorain, and Medina counties

context.text: The Cook Political Report rates the 7th District R+5. Eight Democrats ran in the primary, the most candidates for any Ohio U.S. House district in 2026; Brian Poindexter won with 37.0% of the vote.

Two independent write-in candidates, Thahbia Asad and Andrey Martinichin, are also seeking write-in votes in the general election; they do not appear as printed ballot lines and are not profiled here.

candidates.name: Max Miller
candidates.ballotNote: Incumbent, unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary

summary.text: Miller is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Ohio's 7th District, first elected in 2022. Before Congress he served in the Marine Corps Reserve and worked on Donald Trump's 2016 campaign, in the first Trump administration, and on the 2020 re-election campaign. He serves on the Ways and Means and Foreign Affairs committees and is seeking a third term.

background.text: Grew up in Northeast Ohio and was born in 1988; attended the University of Arizona from 2007 to 2009, then earned a bachelor's degree in history from Cleveland State University in 2013.
Served six years in the U.S. Marine Corps Reserve, according to his House website; Wikipedia reports he joined in 2013, rose to corporal and had no deployments.

Joined Donald Trump's 2016 presidential campaign in February 2016 after working for Marco Rubio's campaign, then held roles in the first Trump administration including confidential assistant at the Treasury Department (2017), lead advance representative in the White House, and associate director of the Presidential Personnel Office.
Was named deputy campaign manager for presidential operations on Trump's 2020 re-election campaign in July 2020 and was appointed to the U.S. Holocaust Memorial Council in December 2020.
Launched a congressional campaign in February 2021; won the May 3, 2022 Republican primary with 71.8% of the vote and the November 2022 general election over Democrat Matthew Diemer with 55.4%.
Won re-election in 2024 over Diemer and independent Dennis Kucinich, and won the 2026 Republican primary unopposed.

In Congress, was chosen by fellow sophomore Republicans to serve on the Republican Steering Committee; sits on the Ways and Means Committee (Oversight and Work and Welfare subcommittees) and the Foreign Affairs Committee, according to his House website.
In January 2023 introduced the resolution, adopted by the House, to remove Rep. Ilhan Omar from the Foreign Affairs Committee.
According to his House website, he lives in Bay Village, Ohio.

record.text: Served on the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology and the Committee on Agriculture during the 118th Congress (2023-2024).

candidates.name: Brian Poindexter
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary with 37.0% in an eight-candidate field

summary.text: Poindexter is the Democratic nominee for Ohio's 7th District. A union ironworker and apprenticeship instructor for Ironworkers Local 17, he was elected to the Brook Park City Council in 2017 and won a crowded Democratic primary on May 5, 2026. He describes his campaign as centered on workers' wages, health care costs and ending corporate money in politics.

background.text: Graduated from John Marshall High School and earned an associate degree from Cuyahoga Community College.
Describes his father as a union machinist and says he started working in a machine shop at 15.
Has worked as a union ironworker and, by his own account, as an ironworker and apprenticeship instructor for about 20 years; as of 2026 he is an apprenticeship instructor for Ironworkers Local 17.
Elected to the Brook Park City Council in 2017 and has served as an at-large member.
Won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary with 37.0% of the vote, ahead of Ed FitzGerald (21.6%) and other candidates.

priorities.text: Campaign website says the economy should be 'built from the foundation up' by workers, criticizing policies he says protect corporate profits over wages.
priorities.quote: An economy that works can't be built from the penthouse down. It has to be built from the foundation up, and workers are that foundation.

priorities.text: Campaign website supports the right to organize and says unions 'raise standards not just for their members, but for entire industries.'
Campaign website says healthcare 'shouldn't disappear when a job does' and calls for healthcare that is portable and not tied to employment.

positions.summary: Campaign website calls for policies that strengthen wages so that working people can 'afford to live with dignity.'
positions.quote: My focus is simple: if you work hard, you should be able to afford to live with dignity, support your family, and plan for the future.

positions.summary: Campaign website calls for healthcare that is 'portable and dependable' and not tied to employment status.
positions.quote: Healthcare should be portable and dependable, so a change in work doesn't turn into a crisis for you or your family.
